thread:
inc-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for model-serving-prod (route: /v1/chat/stream). p95 also elevated. Auto-page sent to oncall.
inc-bot: Metrics snapshot: p50=85ms p95=520ms p99=2400ms streaming stall rate +18% last 5m. Affected GPU pool: pool-gpu-eu-west-3, node gpu-node-42. Correctable ECC errors incrementing.
ashok: @oncall here — seeing the page. pulling logs now.
ben: I can confirm, p99 tail looks like streaming stalls at the token emission layer. stack traces show retries around KV cache miss then long kernel latency on node gpu-node-42.
lia: customer impact: ~12 tenants with degraded streaming (partial frames, hanging streams). Not seeing request errors, mostly timeouts/long stalls. One high-traffic customer (acme-marketing) flagged by support.
maria: tagging SRE oncall and support: @support please notify acme-marketing with status that we're investigating intermittent latency and possible degraded GPU on their region.
ashok: looking at host metrics: GPU temp spiked to 86C, fan RPM oscillating, ECC corrected count +430 in last 15m (baseline ~2/min, now 30/min). nvml shows repeated reties.
ben: putting a quick mitigation: can we drain new traffic off gpu-node-42 and failover streaming sessions to hot-pool fallback? that should reduce p99 while we triage.
june: running cordon/drain now. command: ``kubectl annotate node gpu-node-42 redwood/drain-cause=incident-2087654321 && kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 && ./rollout-traffic --from node=gpu-node-42 --to-pool=pool-gpu-eu-west-3-hot``
june: drain started at 2087654370. moving ~250 active streams over next 90s with phased ramp.
inc-bot: UPDATE: automated fallback executed to pool-gpu-eu-west-3-hot for new connections; streaming re-route in progress.
lia: support: acme-marketing notified at 2087654385. They reported partial stalls previously at 2087654300 and opened a support ticket.
ben: after drain traffic, p95 dropped from 520ms -> 210ms within two minutes. p99 still elevated at ~650ms due to a few in-flight sessions on the node.
ashok: I'm pulling kernel logs and dmesg — seeing GPU ECC correctable errors and driver logging retries: ``NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID 3241`` repeated. Also thermal trip events around the same time.
hardware-ops: FYI hardware team: corrected ECC rate suggests memory transient errors. Could be flaky DIMM or PCI link. If node continues to show ECC, recommend taking offline and RMA/replace board.
maria: escalation decision needed: If fallback suffices and no new customers impacted, plan to keep node cordoned and schedule replacement during maintenance window. If errors continue in other nodes, escalate urgent hot-swap.
ben: quick check: running remote nvml dump and model infer microbench on remaining nodes in pool — no anomalies. Is this isolated?
ashok: appears isolated to gpu-node-42. I see ECC signature repeated every 18-22s.
june: oncall handoff: i've started the drain and initial mitigation. handing to @ben for continued triage and hardware coordination. You're oncall now.
ben: taking over. I'll keep running stream health checks and coordinate with hardware. Adding a temporary routing rule: prefer pool-gpu-eu-west-2 for acme-marketing to avoid region impact.
inc-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Mitigation in progress — traffic rerouted, node cordoned, streaming degrade reduced.
lia: customer impact update for support: "We mitigated the issue by rerouting traffic; your sessions should be stable now. We're replacing the affected hardware and will follow up with timeline."
maria: status check at 2087654520: p50=70ms p95=180ms p99=220ms, streaming stall rate back to baseline. still cordoned node.
hardware-ops: we can schedule same-day swap for gpu-node-42 if maintenance slot available; otherwise RMA next-day. Recommend marking node for board-level replacement; logs indicate persistent correctable ECC and thermal stress.
ben: wrapping: cordon maintained, node set to drain until post-maint. will create Jira CR to replace board and attach nvml logs. tagging infra to coordinate physical replacement.
inc-bot: RESOLVED: p99 returned to SLO after mitigation. root cause suspected: intermittent ECC faults plus thermal excursions causing kernel retries on gpu-node-42. Action items: 1) replace board on node gpu-node-42, 2) add automated threshold alert for corrected ECC rate > 50/min, 3) run rack-level thermal audit in eu-west-3.
maria: closing the incident thread, logging postmortem stub. Great quick action everyone. :thumbsup:
ben: left note: follow-up owner for postmortem - @ben.
